// about: Mapping scheme for the Instance Migrator plugin, authored from the Sample Kit Playground pair below. It covers the case Figma's native swap cannot handle: SLOT content that must be carried across when the slot is both RENAMED (`slot` -> `bottom slot`) and GATED behind a renamed boolean (`Bottom Slot` -> `hasBottomSlot`). Structures were read node-by-node from the live file; see agentNotes for what is verified and for the one plugin-side limitation this file cannot work around.

old.name: Snackbar [deprecated]
old.// sampleInstances: 64801-9444 is the pair originally authored against. 64801-9822 is the instance the maintainer reported as failing to migrate its slot layer; same component, Configuration=Text & action / Two lines / Show close affordance=False, with `stuff` + `Rectangle 1` in the slot.

// map: Old nodePath -> new nodePath, or null to drop. Two slot-related rules apply here, and they pull in opposite directions, so read both. (1) Content the DESIGNER dropped into an old slot (`content/slot/stuff`, `content/slot/Rectangle 1`) must NOT be listed: the plugin flags it `inSlot`, captures it and rebuilds it wholesale, and a map[] entry would make the generic override replay fight that restore. Those are handled by slots[]. (2) A layer that belongs to the NEW COMPONENT'S OWN definition but happens to live under a slot path — `action-slot/Inverse-button/...` — is the opposite case: it is not restored content, it ships with the component, and an explicit map[] entry is exactly how its override gets there. The plugin honours an explicit entry even for an inSlot source, which is what makes the button-label row below work.

map.note: Unchanged path. Listed for self-documentation; it would auto-map. Internal layout differs (old aligns items-start, new centers them) but that is the component's own definition, not an override, so nothing to carry across.
Unchanged path. Carries the snackbar's text override.

map.// notListedInUI: EXPECTED: this target path is NOT selectable from the plugin's dropdown, and that is a plugin limitation, not an error in this row. The UI builds its target list from `comp.createInstance()`, which instantiates the component set's DEFAULT variant — `Configuration=Text only`, which contains no `action-slot` and no `Inverse-button` at all. So the dropdown offers `Supporting text` as its only text layer. The APPLY path is different: it indexes the real swapped instance, which keeps this instance's own `Configuration=Text & action`, so this path genuinely resolves at apply time. Authoring it here is currently the ONLY way to map the button label.
map.note: THE BUTTON LABEL ('Add to Basket'). Mapped explicitly because the path changed: the button was a direct child of the root and now sits inside the `action-slot` SLOT, so identical-path auto-mapping cannot find it. Verified in the live file that the two buttons have IDENTICAL internals — old 64796:7880 and new 64796:8699 are both `Content/State-layer/{Icon, Label}` — so the leaf path lines up exactly and the text override replays cleanly. An earlier revision of this scheme dropped `Inverse-button` outright on the theory that the re-base (`Button - text` -> `Button - tonal`) left nothing to replay onto; that was wrong, and the visible symptom was the label resetting to the new component's default on every migration.

The full-bleed overlay marking the component as deprecated (green, #11FF00 at 50% opacity, absolutely positioned over the whole 344x130 frame). It has no counterpart in the replacement, by design — dropped deliberately.

// props: The variant properties (Configuration, # of lines, Show close affordance) DO match by name and apply automatically. One does not: the boolean gating the bottom slot was renamed `Bottom Slot` -> `hasBottomSlot`. That rename is load-bearing rather than cosmetic — while the boolean is false the SLOT is not in the new tree at all, so the plugin's slot indexer cannot see it and the slots[] entry below has nothing to match against. Without this rename the designer's slot content is silently dropped even though slots[] names it correctly.

renames.note: Old exposes `Bottom Slot` (on in the sample instance); new exposes `hasBottomSlot` (off by default). Matched on base name, so the #id suffixes are stripped automatically — never paste ids here.

// values: Empty on purpose. Every old value has a 1:1 path target in the new tree (see map[]); nothing has to become a property, merge or split.
// slots: Old SLOT path -> new SLOT path. REQUIRED here rather than optional: the plugin auto-matches a slot by identical path, then by unique leaf name, then by being the sole slot on both sides. All three fail for this pair — the paths differ, the leaf names differ (`slot` vs `bottom slot`), and the new component has TWO slots — so without this entry the plugin correctly refuses to guess and reports the slot unmatched.

slots.note: Whatever the designer dropped into the old `slot` is rebuilt into `bottom slot`. This entry DEPENDS ON the props[] rename above: `bottom slot` is gated behind `hasBottomSlot`, and while that boolean is false the slot is not present in the tree for the plugin to match — so the rename must land for this mapping to resolve at all. Placing content does not switch the gate on; the boolean does.

// drop: Old paths whose overrides are knowingly discarded. Silences the 'unmapped' warning and records that it was a decision.
agentNotes: FOURTH PASS 2026-07-31, prompted by the maintainer reporting the button label resetting after migration ('Add to Basket' -> the new component's default). CAUSE WAS THIS FILE, specifically the second-pass decision to drop `Inverse-button` outright. That decision rested on the claim that the re-base from `Button - text` (58650:8094) to `Button - tonal` (58651:11237) left 'no shared structure to replay overrides onto'. That claim is FALSE and was never checked against the file: old button 64796:7880 and new button 64796:8699 have IDENTICAL internals — `Content/State-layer/{Icon, Label}` in both — so the label leaf lines up exactly. The re-base changes the container's fill (transparent -> rgba(232,222,248,0.3)) and height (48 -> 40), which are the component's own definition, not overrides, and do not affect whether a text override can replay. FIX: `Inverse-button` is out of drop[] and map[] now carries the leaf-to-leaf row `Inverse-button/Content/State-layer/Label` -> `action-slot/Inverse-button/Content/State-layer/Label`. Confirmed against the hand-built new instance 64801-9613, where that exact path holds 'Add to Basket'. An explicit map[] entry is honoured even when the TARGET sits under a slot path (code.js gates on `inSlot && !explicit[oldPath]`), and the SOURCE is a root child, so nothing here collides with the slot restore. The label may also be prop-bound; that needs no special handling, since the plugin walks ancestors and routes the write through whichever instance exposes the TEXT property.  ||  THIRD PASS 2026-07-31, prompted by the maintainer reporting instance 64801-9822 still not migrating its slot layer. Read from the live file and now VERIFIED rather than inferred: (a) the old slot is `content/slot` and the new slot is `content/bottom slot`, and BOTH ship `hidden=true` in their component definitions (old variant 64796:7878, new variant 64796:8697) — so the slot being hidden is the component's own default, and it is the per-instance boolean that reveals it; (b) both COMPONENT_SETs expose the SAME three VARIANT axes (Configuration, # of lines, Show close affordance) with identical names and identical value sets, so no variant needs renaming — the gate is a BOOLEAN component property, which is why it does not appear in the variant names; (c) instance 64801-9822 is Configuration=Text & action, # of lines=Two lines, Show close affordance=False, and its slot really does hold two designer-authored layers, `stuff` (text, overridden to three lines of 'Snackbar supporting text') and `Rectangle 1` — these are the layers that go missing; (d) in the NEW component `action-slot` is confirmed a SLOT containing its own `Inverse-button` (74x40), which is why map[] cannot route the old button into it. NOTE the exact `#id` suffixes on the two boolean properties were NOT read (that needs a REST token or the plugin itself), but this does not matter: the plugin matches component properties on BASE name and strips the suffix, so `Bottom Slot` / `hasBottomSlot` as written below is the correct form — never paste ids.  ||  CORRECTED 2026-07-31 (second pass), after the maintainer reported that slot content was NOT being recreated in the new component. Root cause: the bottom-slot boolean is RENAMED between the two components — old `Bottom Slot`, new `hasBottomSlot` — and the previous revision left props[] empty on the stated assumption that every property name matched. It does not. Because the new SLOT is gated behind that boolean, an unwritten gate means the slot is absent from the tree, the plugin's slot indexer cannot see it, and the slots[] entry below silently has nothing to match — the content is dropped even though the mapping names it correctly. props[] now carries the rename. Also corrected: the `Inverse-button` map[] entry pointed INTO the new `action-slot` SLOT, which is not something map[] can express (slot content is owned by the capture/restore pair); it is now an explicit drop.  ||  KNOWN PLUGIN-SIDE LIMITATION, not fixable from this file: the plugin applies root component properties AFTER restoreSlots(), so the renamed gate is written too late to materialise the slot before slots are indexed. Until the apply paths write root props before restoreSlots(), this scheme's rename is correct but the slot restore will still report 'new component has no slot to receive this content'. Verified against the real walkPaths/indexSlots/applyPropsByBaseName logic with a mock figma: with the old order the slot index is EMPTY; with root props written first it contains `content/bottom slot`, and the second props write is a no-op so nothing is double-counted.  ||  RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-31 against the playground instances the maintainer supplied: deprecated = node 64801-9444, replacement = node 64801-9613 (recorded as old.sampleInstance / new.sampleInstance). Those instances resolve to component sets 64796:7861 and 64796:8680 respectively, i.e. the same pair this scheme already targeted. (That pass concluded 'map[], slots[], props[] and values[] all still hold' — superseded by the correction above: props[] did not hold.) Three details were corrected in this pass: (1) the `deprecated` overlay is GREEN (#11FF00 @ 50%), not red as previously written; (2) the action button is not merely reparented, it is re-based onto a DIFFERENT component — `Button - text` (58650:8094, 48px, transparent) becomes `Button - tonal` (58651:11237, 40px, rgba(232,222,248,0.3)) — so only its label survives the swap; (3) `content` switches from items-start to centered, which is component-internal and needs no mapping.  ||  ORIGINALLY VERIFIED from the live file (Sample Kit Playground, zO662vC0476nlRFJg85RBR) via Figma Dev Mode: both subtrees were read node by node. Old = content{Supporting text, slot{stuff, Rectangle 1}}, Inverse-button, deprecated. New = content{Supporting text, bottom slot}, action-slot{Inverse-button}. Both are COMPONENT_SETs with the same 10 variants and identical variant property names.  ||  KEYS ARE REAL, read from GET /v1/files/zO662vC0476nlRFJg85RBR/component_sets: old b00f5e85… (node 64796:7861), new cd1ec1f5… (node 64796:8680). Both node ids match the subtrees inspected above, so the keys and the structure describe the same pair. Note that published keys are NOT obtainable from Dev Mode / the MCP server — only from the REST API with a token, or from inside a plugin.  ||  DELIBERATELY NOT MAPPED: `content/slot/stuff` and `content/slot/Rectangle 1`. They live inside a SLOT, so the plugin flags them `inSlot` and its slot capture/restore pair rebuilds them. Naming them in map[] would override that and make the generic override replay fight the restore. Slot children are handled by slots[], never by map[].
